title: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
authors: Si-Yu Zhang, Meng-Long Song, Hai-Tao Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, Dong Wang
abstract: Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under indepen dent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-assisted slow switching protocol yields a superadditive transient ergotropy gain and near-maximal ergotropy during the initial charging stage, while the no-DM slow-switching control reaches comparable ergotropy only in a later revival. A finite superadditive region persists at fixed RTN amplitude, with protocol-dependent location and gain. In the Ising model, the enhancement is nonmonotonic in DM strength, with intermediate coupling giving near-optimal performance. Dressed-channel analysis associates this enhancement with changes in transition frequencies and longitudinal-noise matrix elements that reduce slow-RTN spectral weight. Superadditivity also persists in the tested anisotropic XY model.
summary: This theoretical study investigates how Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction can synergistically enhance the charging efficiency of a quantum battery when subjected to non-Markovian noise. By employing the Burshtein-Kubo formalism, the authors demonstrate that specific slow-switching protocols yield superadditive gains in ergotropy. This highlights the potential of engineered interactions to overcome environmental decoherence in quantum energy storage.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of protecting quantum batteries (QBs) from environmental noise and investigating how structured environmental memory modifies the charging dynamics.
main_result: DM-assisted slow-switching protocols yield a superadditive transient ergotropy gain during initial charging, outperforming non-DM controls, with optimal performance found at intermediate DM coupling strengths.
method: The study uses the exact Burshtein-Kubo stochastic-Liouville formalism to model the open quantum system dynamics under independent local Random Telegraph Noise (RTN).
model_or_system: The system is a two-spin quantum battery modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating anisotropic Heisenberg interactions and a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling term. The dynamics are governed by coupling to independent RTN environments.
key_observables: Ergotropy, average charging power, and synergy factors ($\eta_{abs}, \eta_{rel}$).
important_parameters: DM coupling strength ($D$), noise amplitude, and charging protocol (fast vs. slow switching).
main_assumptions: The noise is modeled as independent local Random Telegraph Noise (RTN), allowing for an exact Burshtein-Kubo treatment.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the two-qubit open QB model under parallel and collective charging schemes coupled to independent RTN noise. Figure 3 (mentioned in notes) compares ergotropy gains for different charging protocols.
paper_structure: The paper details the model (Hamiltonian, noise coupling) using the Burshtein-Kubo formalism, analyzes performance metrics like ergotropy, and compares various charging protocols (DM-assisted vs. no-DM) in both Ising and anisotropic XY models.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics, providing concrete mechanisms (DM interaction) to enhance energy harvesting in noisy quantum devices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic diagram of the two-qubit open quantum battery model under different charging schemes. The battery consists of two identical two-level systems, initialized in the fully discharged state | ↓↓⟩and driven toward the fully charged state | ↑↑⟩over time t. Both cells are independently driven by a local external charging field Hch with strength Ω, while coupled to localized random tele- graph noise (RTN) environments. Parallel charging scheme: the two cells evolve independently without inter-cell interactions. Collective charging scheme: the cells interact through the internal Hamiltonian Hint.
